raw_papers.title: A Survey of Zero-Shot Learning: Settings, Methods, and Applications
raw_papers.abstract: Zero-shot learning studies recognition of unseen classes by transferring knowledge from seen classes through semantic attributes, language embeddings, or auxiliary descriptions. Survey papers organize the problem settings, datasets, evaluation protocols, and common model families.
raw_papers.summary: Zero-shot learning studies recognition of unseen classes by transferring knowledge from seen classes through semantic attributes, language embeddings, or auxiliary descriptions.

raw_papers.title: Semantic Embedding Approaches for Zero-Shot Image Classification
raw_papers.abstract: This paper introduces semantic embedding models that align image features with class descriptions. The approach provides a foundation for recognizing unseen categories without labeled examples.
raw_papers.summary: This paper introduces semantic embedding models that align image features with class descriptions.

raw_papers.title: Generalized Zero-Shot Learning with Calibrated Stacking
raw_papers.abstract: Generalized zero-shot learning evaluates models on both seen and unseen classes. Calibration methods reduce the bias toward seen classes and improve balanced recognition performance.
raw_papers.summary: Generalized zero-shot learning evaluates models on both seen and unseen classes.

raw_papers.title: Prompt-Based Vision-Language Models for Zero-Shot Recognition
raw_papers.abstract: Large vision-language models enable zero-shot recognition by comparing images with natural language prompts. Prompt engineering and representation alignment are central to recent progress.
raw_papers.summary: Large vision-language models enable zero-shot recognition by comparing images with natural language prompts.

raw_papers.title: Benchmarking Robustness in Zero-Shot Learning Systems
raw_papers.abstract: Robust zero-shot systems must handle distribution shift, ambiguous class descriptions, and dataset bias. Benchmark design is important for evaluating real-world transfer performance.
raw_papers.summary: Robust zero-shot systems must handle distribution shift, ambiguous class descriptions, and dataset bias.
